summary: Ambiguous pin handshake during canary slice results in mixed routing to compatibility fallback
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightAnswers reported mixed responses and tokenization deltas after pinning a model version for their production tenant during our staggered canary rollout. The tenant was explicitly pinned to open-vicuna-13b-v1. During the canary window several requests were routed to a backward-compatible variant (open-vicuna-13b-quantized-v1) resulting in shorter outputs, unexpected token counts, and downstream quality regressions.

Impact:
- Multiple production requests for the tenant received degraded outputs for ~18 minutes.
- Customer observed user-facing quality regressions in a live workflow (search summarization).
- Billing anomalies reported (spike in token counts due to re-tokenization mismatch).

Environment:
- Hosted Redwood Dedicated cluster in us-west serving BrightAnswers dedicated pool.
- Rolling canary for orchestrator v2.7.3 promoting new prewarm logic.

Observed behavior:
- Tenant remained "pinned" in control-plane metadata but edge routing decisions intermittently allowed a compatibility fallback variant.
- Prefetch/prewarm mirror writes appear to have overwritten a route fingerprint for a subset of ingress hosts.

Expected behavior:
- Explicit tenant pin should force all active sessions to the pinned variant until pin released or TTL expired.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Pin tenant t-brightanswers to open-vicuna-13b-v1 via console or API
2) Begin canary promotion of orchestrator v2.7.3 with prewarm mirroring enabled on subset of edge hosts
3) Send concurrent streaming requests that exercise long prompts and embeddings
4) Observe routing and compare model hashes in response headers

comments: 2026-03-10 14:30 - Support (Aisha): Customer reported intermittent short responses; escalated to SRE and assigned to Diego.
2026-03-10 15:05 - SRE (Diego): Reproduced mirror-write event in edge logs; suspect prewarm mirror logic overwrote the route fingerprint used for pin matching.
2026-03-10 16:10 - Customer (BrightAnswers): We saw ~18 minutes of degraded outputs starting at ~14:02 UTC. This affected a live cohort of users. Please advise on rollback and mitigation.
2026-03-11 09:22 - Eng (Li Chen): Adding orchestrator instrumentation PR that adds atomic compare-and-swap for route fingerprint writes: github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/8122
2026-03-12 11:00 - SRE (Diego): Canary paused and rolled back to v2.7.2 for affected hosts; applied hotfix to prevent overwrite during mirror operations. Continue monitoring.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: prewarm mirror writes are non-atomic and can collide with existing route metadata, causing fingerprint mismatch and bypassing pin check.
Checked control-plane snapshot: tenant pin exists and TTL active for t-brightanswers during whole window.
Found edge host edge-19 performed a mirror-write that changed the per-host route fingerprint without updating pin mapping index.
Orchestrator v2.7.3 prewarm mirror uses asynchronous writes which can race with edge-level pin reconciliation. Reproducible when canary slice hits prescaled mirror hosts.
Tokenization deltas likely stem from quantized model variant using a slightly different tokenizer config; fallback routing exposed token mismatch which inflated downstream billing counts.
resolution_notes: Applied immediate mitigations: paused canary, rolled back orchestrator to v2.7.2 on affected edge slice, and deployed hotfix that makes prewarm mirror writes atomic and validates route fingerprint consistency before commit. Notified customer of rollback and provided timeline. Engineering PR #8122 merged and scheduled for controlled relaunch behind feature gate with integration tests. Billing team credited the customer's invoice for the spike pending audit.
postmortem_follow_up: ENG-1234: Add integration test covering pin preservation when prewarm mirror updates route metadata
OPS-4421: Improve telemetry alert for route-fingerprint mismatches with tenant pins
DOCS-58: Update runbook to include immediate rollback steps for canary mirror anomalies
SEC-12: Audit tokenization config parity between variant families and add schema validation on model onboarding
